direction: Long-horizon cross-sectional relative-strength rotation between BTC and ETH with an absolute winner-return cash hurdle.
hypothesis: Lower-frequency relative strength may reduce trading-cost drag compared with previously tested short-horizon rotations. Select the stronger of BTC and ETH over 63/126/252 fully closed UTC daily bars, but stay in USDT unless that winner is above a 0/5/10 percent cumulative-return hurdle.

source_paper.citation: Shi, Y., Li, X., & Zhang, J. (2021). Up or down? Short-term reversal, momentum, and liquidity effects in cryptocurrency markets. International Review of Financial Analysis, 78, 101908. DOI:10.1016/j.irfa.2021.101908.
source_paper.finding_summary: The authors study daily cross-sectional cryptocurrency returns and report that very liquid large-cap assets can show daily momentum even where the broad cross-section exhibits reversal. This motivates a low-turnover BTC/ETH relative-strength allocation screen; their broad-universe result does not validate a two-asset portfolio.

complete_rule: At each OOS UTC day boundary d after the previous daily candle is fully closed, compute BTC and ETH simple returns close[d-1]/close[d-1-L]-1 using L in {63,126,252}. BTC wins exact ties. Target 100 percent of the one 2000-USDT portfolio in the winner only if the winning return is strictly greater than the absolute hurdle {0,0.05,0.10}; otherwise target cash. Trade only when the actual holding asset differs from the target. At d 00:01 one-minute open, sell the full old position first, then if required buy the new winner from remaining USDT; failed legs leave actual holdings/cash unchanged and are retried only when the next daily target still differs. Never backfill missed signals or rebalance an unchanged holding. A switch uses two sequential fills and pays costs on both legs.
allocation: Rotation account has 2000 USDT total. Target raw exposure is {BTC:1,ETH:0,cash:0}, {BTC:0,ETH:1,cash:0}, or {BTC:0,ETH:0,cash:1}; no simultaneous asset holdings, normalization, borrow, yield, or other-account transfers. Static 50/50 hold comparator starts with two separate 1000-USDT sleeves and does not rebalance.

time_boundaries.walk_forward: 12 contiguous fixed 30-day OOS folds; no fitted model/parameter; lookback is strictly trailing prior completed days.
time_boundaries.history_disclosure: This date range has been repeatedly used in repository research, not an untouched final holdout.

execution.signal: Only fully closed daily rows; signal becomes available at new UTC day 00:00 after previous UTC day close.
execution.entry_exit: Historical 1m open at 00:01 UTC (60-second availability delay), full position on target changes; terminal liquidation at end UTC 00:01. Historical minute opens are used only in this research backtest, never as current paper10 fills.
execution.accounting: Existing Decimal kernel fill() and lagged daily cost input implementation.

costs.impact_model: 0.5 * sample_stdev(previous 20 complete UTC daily log returns) * sqrt(order quote budget / previous 20 complete daily quote ADV)
costs.note: No historical L2; half-spread, slippage and square-root impact are estimates. No funding or borrow: spot long-only.

failure_gates.interpretation: Historical validation only; does not imply live/future profit or minute-level risk bounds.

prior_research.nearest_existing_family: spot-cross-sectional-dual-momentum-rotation; previous tested lookbacks were 20/40/60 days and hurdles 0/2/4%. These new 63/126/252 day and 0/5/10% definitions are fingerprint-distinct and were selected before results. Prior short-horizon rotations were rejected.
